questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Spectroscopy, Heterocycles & Biomolecules (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The correct decreasing order of carbonyl stretching frequency ($\tilde{\nu}_{\text{C=O}}$) among the following cyclic ketones is
questions.explanationEn: Decreasing the ring size reduces the internal $\text{C-C(O)-C}$ bond angle, which increases the $p$-character of the endocyclic $\text{C-C}$ bonds and consequently increases the $s$-character of the exocyclic $\text{C=O}$ bond. Greater $s$-character strengthens the carbonyl bond and raises $\tilde{\nu}_{\text{C=O}}$: cyclobutanone ($\sim 1780\text{ cm}^{-1}$) $>$ cyclopentanone ($\sim 1745\text{ cm}^{-1}$) $>$ cyclohexanone ($\sim 1715\text{ cm}^{-1}$) $>$ cycloheptanone ($\sim 1705\text{ cm}^{-1}$).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Spectroscopy, Heterocycles & Biomolecules (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In a conformationally locked cyclohexane ring, the vicinal coupling constant $^3J_{\text{HH}}$ between two adjacent protons follows the order
questions.explanationEn: By the Karplus equation, $^3J_{\text{HH}}$ is largest when the dihedral angle $\phi$ is near $180^\circ$ or $0^\circ$ and smallest near $90^\circ$. In a chair cyclohexane, axial-axial protons have $\phi \approx 180^\circ$ ($J_{aa} \approx 8\text{--}13\text{ Hz}$), whereas axial-equatorial and equatorial-equatorial protons both have $\phi \approx 60^\circ$ ($J_{ae}, J_{ee} \approx 2\text{--}5\text{ Hz}$). Hence $J_{aa} > J_{ae} \approx J_{ee}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Spectroscopy, Heterocycles & Biomolecules (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A monobrominated organic compound ($\text{R-Br}$) exhibits $[\text{M}]$ and $[\text{M}+2]$ peaks in its EI mass spectrum with an approximate relative intensity ratio of
questions.explanationEn: Naturally occurring bromine consists of $^{79}\text{Br}$ ($50.7\%$) and $^{81}\text{Br}$ ($49.3\%$), which are present in nearly a $1:1$ ratio separated by $2\text{ mass units}$. Therefore, a compound containing a single bromine atom displays characteristic $[\text{M}]$ and $[\text{M}+2]$ peaks of almost equal intensity ($1:1$).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Spectroscopy, Heterocycles & Biomolecules (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In the Chichibabin reaction, heating pyridine with sodamide ($\text{NaNH}_2$) in liquid ammonia or an inert solvent followed by aqueous workup yields predominantly
questions.explanationEn: The Chichibabin reaction is a nucleophilic aromatic substitution ($\text{S}_\text{N}\text{Ar}$) on the $\pi$-deficient pyridine ring. The amide nucleophile ($\text{NH}_2^-$) attacks the electron-deficient C-2 position (assisted by coordination of $\text{Na}^+$ to the ring nitrogen), forming a Meisenheimer-type adduct that eliminates hydride ($\text{H}^-$, evolving $\text{H}_2$ gas) to afford 2-aminopyridine after workup.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Spectroscopy, Heterocycles & Biomolecules (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following disaccharides is a NON-REDUCING sugar and fails to undergo mutarotation in aqueous solution?
questions.explanationEn: Sucrose is $\alpha$-D-glucopyranosyl-$(1\to 2)$-$\beta$-D-fructofuranoside, in which both anomeric carbons (C-1 of glucose and C-2 of fructose) are locked in the glycosidic bond. Because it lacks a free hemiacetal or hemiketal group, sucrose cannot open to a free carbonyl form, is non-reducing, and does not mutarotate, unlike maltose, lactose, and cellobiose.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Spectroscopy, Heterocycles & Biomolecules (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The correct statement(s) regarding broadband proton-decoupled $^{13}\text{C}$ NMR and DEPT spectroscopy is(are)
optionsEn: Quaternary carbons appear in broadband proton-decoupled $^{13}\text{C}$ NMR spectra but are absent in DEPT-90 and DEPT-135 spectra
In DEPT-135 spectra, $\text{CH}_2$ carbons have opposite phase (pointing down) relative to $\text{CH}$ and $\text{CH}_3$ carbons (pointing up)
Carbonyl carbons of ketones and aldehydes typically resonate downfield in the region $\delta\; 190\text{--}220\text{ ppm}$
Signal areas in routine broadband proton-decoupled $^{13}\text{C}$ NMR spectra are strictly proportional to the number of carbon atoms
questions.explanationEn: (A) True: DEPT relies on polarization transfer from directly attached protons, so quaternary carbons give no DEPT signal. (B) True: DEPT-135 distinguishes $\text{CH}_2$ (negative/down) from $\text{CH}$ and $\text{CH}_3$ (positive/up). (C) True: Aldehyde and ketone carbonyls resonate at $\delta\; 190\text{--}220\text{ ppm}$. (D) False: Routine $^{13}\text{C}$ NMR intensities are NOT strictly quantitative because of variable nuclear Overhauser enhancement (NOE) and long spin-lattice relaxation times ($T_1$) of quaternary carbons.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Spectroscopy, Heterocycles & Biomolecules (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The correct statement(s) regarding the reactivity of furan, pyrrole, and thiophene is(are)
optionsEn: All three undergo electrophilic aromatic substitution preferentially at the C-2 ($\alpha$) position
Furan readily acts as a diene in Diels-Alder $[4+2]$ cycloadditions with reactive dienophiles such as maleic anhydride
Pyrrole reacts with strong mineral acids to undergo rapid polymerization rather than simple stable salt formation
Thiophene undergoes Diels-Alder reactions more readily than furan due to its lower aromaticity
questions.explanationEn: (A) True: C-2 electrophilic attack generates a $\sigma$-complex with three resonance contributors versus only two for C-3 attack. (B) True: Because furan has the lowest aromatic stabilization energy ($\sim 16\text{ kcal mol}^{-1}$), it readily acts as a $4\pi$ diene in Diels-Alder reactions. (C) True: Protonation of pyrrole occurs at C-2 to give an electrophilic iminium ion that rapidly polymerizes (pyrrole red). (D) False: Thiophene has the highest aromaticity ($\sim 29\text{ kcal mol}^{-1}$) and resists normal Diels-Alder cycloaddition.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Spectroscopy, Heterocycles & Biomolecules (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Using the Woodward-Fieser rules, the calculated $\lambda_{\max}$ (in $\text{nm}$) of $1,2$-dimethylcyclohexa-$1,3$-diene is _____ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: $1,2$-Dimethylcyclohexa-$1,3$-diene is a homoannular conjugated diene (base value $= 253\text{ nm}$). The diene chromophore (C1=C2-C3=C4) is attached to $2$ ring residues (C6 at C1 and C5 at C4: $2 \times 5 = 10\text{ nm}$) and $2$ alkyl (methyl) substituents (at C1 and C2: $2 \times 5 = 10\text{ nm}$), with no exocyclic double bond. Thus $\lambda_{\max} = 253 + 10 + 10 = 273\text{ nm}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Spectroscopy, Heterocycles & Biomolecules (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The index of hydrogen deficiency (double bond equivalents, DBE) of an alkaloid with molecular formula $\text{C}_{11}\text{H}_{13}\text{NO}_2$ is _____ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: The index of hydrogen deficiency (DBE) for a neutral molecule $\text{C}_c\text{H}_h\text{N}_n\text{O}_o\text{X}_x$ is $\text{DBE} = c - \frac{h + x}{2} + \frac{n}{2} + 1$. Substituting $c = 11$, $h = 13$, $n = 1$, and $x = 0$ gives $\text{DBE} = 11 - \frac{13}{2} + \frac{1}{2} + 1 = 11 - 6 + 1 = 6$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Spectroscopy, Heterocycles & Biomolecules (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The total number of acyclic stereoisomers possible for an aldohexose ($\text{HOCH}_2(\text{CHOH})_4\text{CHO}$) is _____ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: An acyclic aldohexose possesses $4$ distinct chiral centers (C-2, C-3, C-4, and C-5) and no internal plane of symmetry because the terminal groups ($-\text{CHO}$ and $-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$) are different. Therefore, the total number of stereoisomers is $2^4 = 16$ ($8$ D-sugars and $8$ L-sugars).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Spectroscopy, Heterocycles & Biomolecules (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: An unknown compound $\text{C}_4\text{H}_6\text{O}_3$ exhibits two strong, closely spaced IR bands at $1825\text{ cm}^{-1}$ and $1755\text{ cm}^{-1}$, and no absorption above $3100\text{ cm}^{-1}$. The functional group present in this compound is most likely
questions.explanationEn: Carboxylic acid anhydrides ($\text{R-CO-O-CO-R}$, such as acetic anhydride $\text{C}_4\text{H}_6\text{O}_3$) show two coupled carbonyl stretching bands (symmetric and antisymmetric stretches) separated by $\sim 60\text{--}70\text{ cm}^{-1}$ near $1820\text{ cm}^{-1}$ and $1750\text{ cm}^{-1}$. Absence of a broad $\text{O-H}$ band above $3100\text{ cm}^{-1}$ rules out carboxylic acids and enols, while a lactone shows only a single $\text{C=O}$ band.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Spectroscopy, Heterocycles & Biomolecules (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: A cyclic ketone $\text{C}_7\text{H}_{12}\text{O}$ shows $6$ signals in its broadband proton-decoupled $^{13}\text{C}$ NMR spectrum. Its DEPT-135 spectrum shows $1$ upward signal and $3$ downward signals, while its DEPT-90 spectrum shows $0$ signals. The structure of this ketone is
questions.explanationEn: Zero signals in DEPT-90 rules out all isomers containing a methine ($\text{CH}$) carbon ($2,5$-dimethylcyclopentanone, $3$-methylcyclohexanone, and $4$-methylcyclohexanone all have $\text{CH}$ carbons). In $2,2$-dimethylcyclopentan-$1$-one, the $6$ distinct $^{13}\text{C}$ signals consist of $2$ quaternary carbons (C1=O and C2, absent in DEPT), $3$ non-equivalent $\text{CH}_2$ carbons (C3, C4, C5, pointing down in DEPT-135), and $1$ pair of equivalent $-\text{CH}_3$ carbons (pointing up in DEPT-135).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Spectroscopy, Heterocycles & Biomolecules (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: An aliphatic amine $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NHCH}_3$ ($M = 73$) undergoes predominant $\alpha$-cleavage in EI mass spectrometry. The resulting base peak appears at $m/z$ equal to
questions.explanationEn: In aliphatic amines, the dominant EI-MS fragmentation is $\alpha$-cleavage next to nitrogen with loss of the LARGEST alkyl radical to form a resonance-stabilized iminium ion ($\text{R}_2\text{N}^+=\text{CH}_2$). For $N$-methylpropan-$1$-amine ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2\text{NHCH}_3$, $M = 73$), cleavage of the $\text{C}_\alpha\text{--C}_\beta$ bond expels an ethyl radical ($\text{C}_2\text{H}_5^\bullet$, $29\text{ Da}$) to yield $[\text{CH}_2=\text{NHCH}_3]^+$ at $m/z = 73 - 29 = 44$ (an even-electron ion of even mass due to 1 N atom).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Spectroscopy, Heterocycles & Biomolecules (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: When $4$-nitropyridine $N$-oxide is treated with acetyl chloride ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCl}$) followed by $\text{PCl}_3$, the major product obtained is
questions.explanationEn: In $4$-nitropyridine $N$-oxide, the $N$-oxide activates the ring toward both electrophilic and nucleophilic substitution at C-4. Treatment with $\text{CH}_3\text{COCl}$ ($O$-acylation) generates an $N$-acetoxypyridinium intermediate in which $\text{Cl}^-$ readily displaces the $-\text{NO}_2$ group via $\text{S}_\text{N}\text{Ar}$ to give $4$-chloropyridine $N$-oxide. Subsequent deoxygenation with $\text{PCl}_3$ cleanly yields **$4$-chloropyridine**.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Spectroscopy, Heterocycles & Biomolecules (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In a ribonucleoside such as adenosine, the glycosidic bond connecting the purine base (adenine) to the D-ribose sugar is specifically a
questions.explanationEn: In natural RNA and DNA nucleosides, purine bases (adenine and guanine) are attached via their $N^9$ nitrogen to the anomeric C-1' carbon of D-ribofuranose (or $2'$-deoxy-D-ribofuranose) in the $\beta$-configuration (cis to the C-4' $-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ group). Pyrimidine bases (cytosine, uracil, thymine) are attached via their $N^1$ nitrogen.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Spectroscopy, Heterocycles & Biomolecules (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following compounds can undergo a **retro-Diels-Alder (rDA)** fragmentation in EI mass spectrometry?
questions.explanationEn: A retro-Diels-Alder fragmentation requires a six-membered ring containing at least one endocyclic double bond (cyclohexene moiety) to cleave into a conjugated diene and an alkene. Cyclohexene ($\to$ butadiene + ethene), tetralin ($\to$ *o*-quinodimethane + ethene), and limonene ($\to$ two isoprene units) all possess a cyclohexene-like ring and undergo diagnostic rDA cleavage. Saturated cyclohexane lacks the required double bond.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Spectroscopy, Heterocycles & Biomolecules (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: The reaction(s) of **pyrrole** or **$1H$-indole** that proceed(s) cleanly without acid-induced polymerization is(are)
optionsEn: Vilsmeier-Haack formylation of pyrrole using $\text{DMF}/\text{POCl}_3$ followed by aqueous workup to give pyrrole-$2$-carbaldehyde
Mannich reaction of $1H$-indole with $\text{HCHO}$ and $\text{Me}_2\text{NH}$ in AcOH to give gramine ($3$-((dimethylamino)methyl)-$1H$-indole)
Treatment of pyrrole with $\text{CHCl}_3$ and aqueous $\text{KOH}$ (Reimer-Tiemann reaction) yielding both pyrrole-$2$-carbaldehyde and $3$-chloropyridine
Direct nitration of pyrrole using concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$ and concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ at $80\,^\circ\text{C}$
questions.explanationEn: (A) True: Mild Vilsmeier-Haack formylation selectively gives pyrrole-$2$-carbaldehyde in high yield. (B) True: Mild Mannich aminomethylation of indole selectively yields gramine at C-3. (C) True: Alkaline Reimer-Tiemann conditions avoid acid polymerization and produce pyrrole-$2$-carbaldehyde along with ring-expanded $3$-chloropyridine (Ciamician-Dennstedt pathway). (D) False: Concentrated $\text{HNO}_3/\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ destroys/polymerizes pyrrole; mild acetyl nitrate ($	ext{AcONO}_2$) at low temperature is required.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Spectroscopy, Heterocycles & Biomolecules (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Using the Woodward-Fieser rules (with $\beta\text{-OR} = +30\text{ nm}$), the calculated $\lambda_{\max}$ (in $\text{nm}$) of $3$-ethoxy-$2$-methylcyclohex-$2$-en-$1$-one in ethanol is _____ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: For $3$-ethoxy-$2$-methylcyclohex-$2$-en-$1$-one: base value for a 6-membered cyclic enone $= 215\text{ nm}$; $\alpha$-methyl substituent at C-2 $= +10\text{ nm}$; $\beta$-alkoxy ($-\text{OEt}$) auxochrome at C-3 $= +30\text{ nm}$; $\beta$-ring residue (C-4 attached to C-3) $= +12\text{ nm}$. Total $\lambda_{\max} = 215 + 10 + 30 + 12 = 267\text{ nm}$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Spectroscopy, Heterocycles & Biomolecules (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: In the EI mass spectrum of heptan-$3$-one ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, $M = 114$), the intense even-mass fragment ion formed via McLafferty rearrangement appears at $m/z =$ _____ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: Heptan-$3$-one has $\gamma$-hydrogens on C-6 of the butyl chain. In the McLafferty rearrangement, $\gamma$-hydrogen transfer to the carbonyl oxygen and $\text{C}_4\text{--C}_5$ bond cleavage expel a neutral molecule of propene ($\text{C}_3\text{H}_6$, $42\text{ Da}$) to yield the enol radical cation $[\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C(OH)=CH}_2]^{+\bullet}$ at $m/z = 114 - 42 = 72$.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CY Topic • Organic Spectroscopy, Heterocycles & Biomolecules (Set 02)
questions.questionTextEn: Calculate the nominal molecular mass (in $\text{Da}$) of the linear pentapeptide $\text{Gly-Ala-Val-Leu-Gly}$. (Given nominal molar masses of free amino acids: $\text{Gly} = 75$, $\text{Ala} = 89$, $\text{Val} = 117$, $\text{Leu} = 131$; $\text{H}_2\text{O} = 18$.) Answer: _____ (in integer).
questions.explanationEn: Forming a linear pentapeptide from $5$ free amino acids creates $4$ peptide bonds with the condensation loss of $4$ molecules of water ($4 \times 18 = 72\text{ Da}$). Summing the free amino acid masses: $75 + 89 + 117 + 131 + 75 = 487\text{ Da}$. Subtracting $72\text{ Da}$ gives $487 - 72 = 415\text{ Da}$.
